- When sentiment is consistently positive (≥0.6) over recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast by 1–3% for next period.
- After sharp price spikes (e.g., >5% from prior day), model often overshoots; apply a “cool-down” correction: subtract 2–5% from forecast 2–3 days post-spike.
- If sentiment is negative (≤0.4) and prices are trending down, model frequently underestimates; add 1–3% to forecast to account for mean reversion.
- Model tends to overreact to sentiment shifts — especially when sentiment drops sharply — leading to premature price corrections; delay forecast adjustment by 1–2 days if sentiment turns negative.
- For 30-day horizon, model often fails to capture mean reversion in 10–15 day windows; apply a “reversion bias” correction: if price is above 20-day moving average, reduce forecast by 1–2% per day until it aligns.
- When sentiment is mixed (0.4–0.6) and price is volatile, model overfits short-term noise; use a smoothing filter (e.g., 5-day average) to dampen forecast swings.
